project.title: Good Llama
project.medium: Hand drawing, HTML & CSS 3D, AI animation
project.content:
Good morning, good llama.

A hand-drawn llama – black, with fine outlines and patches of deep blue – inside a ring of teal lettering, and it looks at you: move the mouse anywhere on the page and it turns its head to follow. There is only the one drawing, seen from the front, so the turn is built from depth: the ears sit furthest back, the eyes in the middle and the snout closest, and as the head turns, the nearer parts swing further. Left alone, it sways and blinks.

The drawing was first made as a gift. Before the live version came a five-second turnaround loop animated with AI, in a vertical 9:16 phone format.

caseStudy.challenge: Turn a flat drawing, made as a gift, into something that looks back at you – without 3D software and without redrawing it from other angles.

decisions.title: Depth from layers
decisions.text: The drawing is split into layers – ears, eyes, brow, snout – each placed at its own depth with CSS 3D. When the head turns toward the pointer, the near parts swing further than the far ones, and a single front view reads as a real turn.

decisions.title: Small signs of life
decisions.text: Left alone it sways and blinks, the pupils follow the pointer, and on a phone a tap is where it looks – so it works without a mouse too.

decisions.title: From video to live piece
decisions.text: The first version was a five-second turnaround animated with AI. The live version replaced it because it feels like an interactive pop-up book in digital form – flat layers that come alive when you move, like Cyclos, my pop-up book in paper.

caseStudy.result: A lightweight interactive page in plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, shown live on this page and on desktop and phone alike.
